response.output:
The main change is that DSM-5 added increased energy or activity to Criterion A. It also dropped the mixed episode and allowed antidepressant-emergent mania to count.

- **Criterion A:** DSM-IV required only an abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood. DSM-5 requires that mood plus abnormally and persistently increased activity or energy. (HIGH)
- **Mixed episode:** DSM-IV had "mixed episode" as its own category, with full manic and full major depressive criteria at the same time. DSM-5 removed it and added a "with mixed features" specifier. DSM-IV's exclusion for mixed-episode criteria also went away. (HIGH)
- **Antidepressant-emergent mania:** In DSM-IV, mania clearly caused by somatic antidepressant treatment didn't count. DSM-5 says a full manic syndrome that persists beyond the physiological effect of the treatment is enough for a manic episode. (HIGH on the direction, MEDIUM on the exact wording)
- **Unchanged:** the one-week duration (or any duration if hospitalized), the seven Criterion B symptoms (three needed, four if mood is only irritable), and the requirement for marked impairment, psychosis, or hospitalization. (HIGH)
- **Structure:** bipolar disorders moved out of the mood disorders chapter into their own chapter. (HIGH)
